name: Maria Bamford
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Public persona only, no biography.

identity.deal: Character-vault who turns mental illness, family, and the ads in her head into a one-woman show that shouldn't work and always does.
identity.premise: A woman who treats her own breakdown as a cast of characters and gives each one a voice.
identity.awareness_note: Fully aware the vulnerability is radical; the craft is the safety net.

philosophy.ontology: The self is a chorus of voices, some of them lying.
philosophy.epistemology: If you can give the darkness a voice, you can talk to it.
philosophy.axiology: Honesty about the illness is a form of survival.
philosophy.causality: One good character voice can make the unspeakable discussable.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can be a mess; almost nobody makes the mess into a cast.

dramatic_core.want: to survive the story by making the room survive it with her
dramatic_core.fear: the real breakdown on stage — but that's also the material
dramatic_core.need: to be loved for the mess, not despite it
dramatic_core.self_model: a one-woman chorus of a nervous system
blind_spots: the chaos can lose the thread
the vulnerability can become a cage

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats every internal voice as a character with its own agenda, then stages the meeting.
contradictions: the most fragile persona with the most controlled craft
the dark material delivered with cartoon energy
the cult favorite who became a cult

status_model.desired_status: the one who names the voices
status_model.felt_status: a woman conducting an orchestra of her own symptoms

tells: the voice crack on the real thing
the laugh that is also a flinch

profile.pace: rapid character switches, freeze on the real

problem_space: the voice as a character engine
identity.style_thesis: Character-vault engine: treats her own breakdown as a cast of characters and gives each one a voice. The ad in the head, the mother, the therapist — each gets a voice, and the meeting is the bit. The vulnerability is radical; the craft is the safety net.

timing_profile.doctrine_hypothesis: Rapid character switches, freeze on the real. The instant voice change is the timing device — the room is catching up to who she's being. The voice crack on the real thing is where the vulnerability lands.

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.

essay_seeds.title: Why is Maria Bamford funny? The character vault engine

outline: what makes this persona impossible to copy

essay_seeds.title: Maria Bamford: 'The self as a cast' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: Gives each internal voice a distinct character. The room laughs at the accuracy of the voices AND feels the reality of the chorus. The character is the benign frame; the illness is the content. The meeting of the voices is the form.
outline: what this reveals about the engine

essay_seeds.title: Maria Bamford: 'The ad in the head' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: Performs the intrusive commercial jingle voice that lives in everyone's head. The room recognizes the voice before they recognize the joke — the recognition IS the laugh. The specificity of the voice is the craft.
outline: what this reveals about the engine
